request.prompt: Create original high-quality hand-painted rendered isometric RPG NORMAL monster SALAMANDER (사라만다): a stocky LOW FOUR-LEGGED volcanic fire lizard, red-orange scales with charcoal dorsal plates, broad reptile head, small swept-back horns, four muscular legs with hooked toes, thick attached tail curled close beside body. No external flames or particles; fire is suggested by ember-colored scales only. Clearly a grounded quadruped, never a human, bird or winged dragon. Maintain ONE canonical body anatomy/scale/palette in every pose; detailed readable 78px-game-size silhouette. Orthographic fixed elevated camera with eight truly different compass views, no mirroring. EXACTLY SIXTEEN complete connected figures, FOUR columns FOUR rows. Row1 EAST, head toward screen RIGHT, profile. Row2 SOUTHEAST, head toward lower RIGHT, front-right three-quarter. Row3 SOUTH, chest and snout toward image BOTTOM, front. Row4 SOUTHWEST, head toward lower LEFT, front-left three-quarter. In EACH direction row the FOUR columns are four DISTINCT RUN/TROT phases: 0 front-right + rear-left diagonal paws PLANT, other diagonal lifts; 1 first diagonal pushes off, opposite diagonal swings FORWARD, back flexes; 2 front-LEFT + rear-RIGHT diagonal paws LAND and bear weight, first diagonal lifts; 3 opposite diagonal pushes off and first diagonal swings forward ready for phase0. Change which diagonal bears weight; bend shoulders/elbows/hips/hocks; head remains attached and stable; tail reacts with modest follow-through. No four rigid copies. Keep all four limbs attached, rear-leg silhouette clear in rear views. Same one physical scale for ALL16, directional foreshortening allowed. Bodies and entire curled tail small inside CENTRAL HALF of each equal cell with huge transparent gutters. One solid connected silhouette per cell, full bounding rectangles completely disjoint. No floor/shadows/glow/text/grid/specks/detached pieces. True alpha0 transparent background. Native new run artwork from brief, no original game asset claim. Save local PNG.
